function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has fascinated humans for millennia. Here’s a quick timeline of key figures who helped uncover its secrets:

| Era | Scientist | Contribution |
|-----|-----------|--------------|
| **Ancient Greece** | Thales of Miletus (c. 600 BCE) | First recorded observation of static electricity (rubbing amber). |
| **16th–17th Century** | William Gilbert (1544–1603) | Coined the term *electricus* (from Greek *elektron*, amber) and distinguished between magnetism and static electricity. |
| **18th Century** | Benjamin Franklin (1706–1790) | Conducted the famous kite experiment, proving that lightning is electrical and introduced the concepts of positive/negative charge. |
| **Late 18th Century** | Alessandro Volta (1745–1827) | Invented the voltaic pile (the first battery), demonstrating that chemical reactions can produce a steady electric current. |
| **19th Century** | Michael Faraday (1791–1867) | Discovered electromagnetic induction, laying the groundwork for electric generators and motors. |
| **19th Century** | James Clerk Maxwell (1831–1879) | Unified electricity and magnetism into a single theory of electromagnetism. |

So while no single “discoverer” exists, the cumulative work of these pioneers—and many others—led to our modern understanding of electricity.
